value: A professional, scientific diagram in the style of a top-tier conference, flat 2D vector illustration, academic and clean, no 3D shading, no photorealism, designed for a KDD paper on time series anomaly detection. Section 1 (Left): show the input as a multivariate time series $X \in R^{T\times d}$ using neatly stacked narrow sequence bands aligned to a strict grid, followed immediately by a separate rounded-rectangle module labeled Instance Normalization, then a second rounded-rectangle module labeled Channel Independence + Patching, where the internal visual language indicates per-channel processing and segmented patches without using any figurative metaphor. The left section must preserve the exact preprocessing order and make the text placeholders highly legible with high-contrast typography, concise academic labels, and precise dimension annotations in LaTeX format. Section 2 (Middle): create the largest and most visually dominant module, labeled Dual Attention Contrastive Structure, enclosed by a subtle light-gray or very pale blue grouping frame. Inside, split the flow symmetrically into two rigorously aligned parallel branches receiving the same patched input: an upper Patch-wise Branch that models dependencies among patches with multi-head self-attention and outputs patch-wise representation, and a lower In-patch Branch that models dependencies within each patch and outputs in-patch representation. The two branches must look structurally homologous rather than like unrelated towers, using rounded rectangles for algorithm blocks and narrow segmented strips for sequence or patch representations. Explicitly mark Shared Weights between the two branches using a small centered label with dashed auxiliary connectors or a bracket-style annotation, making clear that it is a parameter-sharing constraint rather than a data-flow path. Integrate the multi-scale design inside this middle section, not as a post-processing add-on: for each branch, represent multiple patch sizes as small parallel subpaths or aligned repeated mini-blocks that merge back into one branch output, using restrained brightness variations within the same academic blue family instead of saturated multicolor coding. All modules and submodules must be aligned to a grid system, evenly spaced, uncluttered, and balanced with generous white space. Section 3 (Middle-Right): place an Upsampling / Alignment area directly after the two branches and before any discrepancy computation, with one aligned module on the upper path labeled patch-to-point repeat and one aligned module on the lower path labeled point-to-patch repeat, emphasizing that both outputs must be brought to comparable granularity before comparison. Then merge both aligned representations into a central Representation Discrepancy block, visually emphasized with a slightly stronger border. Around or inside this block, include compact formula annotations in LaTeX such as $L=\frac{1}{2}D(P,\mathrm{Stopgrad}(N))+\frac{1}{2}D(N,\mathrm{Stopgrad}(P))$ and indicate Bidirectional KL Divergence as the comparison mechanism. Use thin bidirectional comparison marks only in this discrepancy zone to express mutual discrepancy, while keeping the main computation flow as unidirectional solid arrows. Above or adjacent to this discrepancy block, add a secondary training-only label or small module named Contrastive Training Loss connected with dashed lines, clearly separating training supervision from inference output. Section 4 (Right): from the discrepancy block, continue the inference path with a solid left-to-right chain of Point-wise Anomaly Score, Threshold $\delta$, and Binary Prediction $Y$, all strictly aligned and visually clean. The anomaly-related nodes should use restrained low-saturation red accents through border highlights or small warning markers, while normal/reference semantics, if shown, may use muted teal sparingly; do not rely on color alone to encode meaning, also use labels and shape emphasis. The final prediction node should distinguish abnormal and normal outcomes with academic restraint, without decorative icons. Use a white or extremely light gray background, flat fills, thin clean borders, Arial or Helvetica-like sans serif typography, semibold section titles, readable placeholder text, and consistent font hierarchy suitable for a two-column paper figure. Include a compact legend area if space permits, styled consistently and aligned to the same grid, explaining rounded rectangle = model block, narrow strip = time-series or patches, blue solid arrow = main computation flow, gray or blue-gray dashed connector = shared weights or training constraint, bidirectional comparison marker = discrepancy relation, red accent = anomaly-related output, and parallel mini-blocks = multi-scale patch sizes. The entire composition must feel precise, highly abstract, and publication-ready, with no reconstruction decoder, no cartoon elements, no clouds, no biological metaphors, no ornamental textures, no shadows, no perspective distortion, no messy crossings, and no visually ambiguous arrows; preserve the main logic of preprocessing to dual-view representation learning to representation discrepancy to anomaly decision, while clearly distinguishing training and inference semantics within a single coherent architecture figure.
